title: Ben Johnson on bringing relentless attitude every week | Press Conference
headline: Johnson previews a short-week Thursday game vs. New England and praises Caleb Williams' Sunday performance; no injury news given.
summary: Johnson opened by saying the team is installing the game plan for a short week and a Thursday game against New England, which he called a physical, well-coached opponent led by a coach-of-the-year head coach. On Caleb Williams, he dismissed the idea that Williams had improved by sitting or watching from the sideline, saying the same growth was visible in camp, and he said the key is stringing good performances together. He described New England's defense as talented up front, especially on the inside, with strong linebackers and edge players, and noted Kevin Byard's fit in their scheme and Christian Gonzalez's unclear alignment. On the offense, he said Drake Maye combines an elite deep ball with running ability, and that Josh McDaniels keeps the offense putting up points. He credited Dennis Allen's defensive pressure package, especially on third down, and said players understand the system better in year two. On special teams and the overall Sunday win, he stressed that swarming, ball security, and takeaways must become a weekly standard rather than a one-week spike. He closed by saying the team must play clean, after a high-penalty game last week, to beat a good opponent on a short week.

signals.claim: Williams put together a good performance Sunday and the team wants to string consistent performances together
signals.note: Coach praised his recent play and downplayed any idea that his development came from sitting out, so the current form looks secure heading into a short-week game.
signals.quote: he put together a good performance and the key with him

topics.detail: Johnson credited coordinator Dennis Allen's third-down pressure package and said players understand the system better this year, with more tight coverage and less room for the quarterback to escape.
Johnson highlighted nine players to the ball on several special-teams plays and wants swarming, ball security, and takeaways every week, not just a one-game effort.
Johnson called New England's front seven difficult to move, with a challenge for the tackles, and said Drake Maye and Josh McDaniels' offense are scoring in bunches on a three-game winning streak.

title: Campbell on Week 7 preparation
headline: Brian Branch is returning to the lineup, and Campbell says Keith Abney will keep playing, so the safety depth chart is set to shift.
summary: Campbell called Green Bay a very good, playing-well-right-now team, citing their plus-six turnover margin, their opportunistic defense, and Jordan Love as the driver of the offense. He flagged Matthew Golden and Christian Watson as dangerous deep threats, with about half of their deep targets resulting in either DPI or a catch. He said the Packers will lean on the run game, expects Josh Jacobs back, and described Love's ability to extend plays as the key threat his front has to limit. On the Packers' coaching, he said they will likely keep their core concepts and just add wrinkles. Campbell said Skyler Gill-Howard's edge rush was a one-off he didn't expect to see much of going forward, though he praised his versatility and professionalism. He said division games matter a lot, and that this one is the first divisional game at home this season. On the safety spot, he said Brian Branch is returning, that Chuck Clark has been steady, and that Keith Abney is worth continuing to invest in. He said Branch's versatility lets him play high or underneath and gives the staff flexibility with the other safety. He also gave an update on the player referred to as Kirby, saying he is doing well and is in a good headspace, but he gave no timetable.

injuries.detail: Campbell said Branch is coming back, which creates a decision at the other safety spot.

signals.claim: Branch is returning to the lineup for Week 7 and gives the defense flexibility at safety.
signals.note: A return for a versatile safety adds a usable IDP and defensive piece back to the lineup.
signals.quote: Here's what's great about getting BB.

signals.claim: Abney will play for Detroit and is worth continuing to invest in.
signals.note: Campbell's endorsement suggests Abney could have a meaningful role in the safety rotation, though Branch's return may cut into it.
signals.quote: Abney is is worth continuing to invest in.

signals.claim: Clark will be where he is supposed to be and remains a steady veteran in the safety rotation.
signals.note: Clark's role depends on how the safety snaps split once Branch returns.
signals.quote: Chuck has been really steady for us, man.

signals.claim: Gill-Howard will not see a heavy dose of edge rushing going forward.
signals.note: His recent edge work was described as a curveball, so his rush snaps are unlikely to grow.
signals.quote: I don't think you're going to see some heavy dose of him out there.

topics.detail: Campbell expects Love, Golden and Watson to create big plays, and says the Packers will look to establish the run with Josh Jacobs, who is expected back.

Campbell said the Packers' defense has been opportunistic and disguises well, with seven takeaways over the last two games, and Detroit's staff is reviewing past games for clues on how they may attack.
Campbell emphasized the importance of division games, noting Detroit went 2-4 in division last year and that this is the first divisional home game this season.
Campbell said the player referred to as Kirby is doing well, gave no return timetable, and was not identifiable on the provided roster.

title: Shanahan Reflects on 6-0 Start, Gritty Finish Over Commanders
headline: Mike Evans (Achilles tendinitis) is questionable after leaving early, Demarcus Robinson won't play this week, and Romello Height and Ashtyn Davis earned bigger roles in the win.
summary: Shanahan said Mike Evans's Achilles tendinitis, which had bothered him all week, flared up during the game and kept him out after the first half. He described it as soreness rather than something needing more testing, and said Evans felt confident enough to play but the coach knew he might not last. Shanahan was frustrated by three-and-outs and penalties that stalled the offense in the second half, while praising the defense for holding on despite losing Upton Stout and Luke Gifford. He said Romello Height had a big impact, and Ashtyn Davis stepped in at corner and played pivotal snaps in the fourth quarter. On Christian McCaffrey, he said the team used him in the slot and at receiver to mix up receiver options. He said Demarcus Robinson won't be ready this week, and that a Deebo Samuel return is possible around the bye week. He also said a receiver returning from a long injury is expected back soon and the team has enough depth for now. Shanahan closed by saying he was proud of the team's competitive stamina in finishing the 6-0 start.

title: HC Dan Quinn | 10/21/26
headline: Terry McLaurin is out for the season with a torn patellar tendon, and Dan Quinn expects Van Jefferson and other receivers to take on bigger roles.
summary: Quinn opened by saying captain Terry McLaurin tore his patellar tendon, will have surgery, and is out for the rest of the season, which he called a gut punch. He described the team's first six games as adversity-filled and said the reset and response are what he is focused on during the bye. Quinn praised the second half against San Francisco as much stronger than the first half and said getting the whole game in sync is the key. He said the offensive line performance fell below the standard he expects and that the staff will keep searching for the right interior combination. He said the bye will be used for a self-scout to streamline the playbook into a smaller set of things the team can execute, with tweaks rather than a new system. On defense, he wants better pre-snap communication and fewer explosive pass plays. On Jayden Daniels, he said the offense will be better when Daniels is fully back and expects more keepers and out-of-pocket plays off play action. He said injury updates on other players, including Javon and Treylon Burks, would come Monday after more imaging.

injuries.detail: Torn patellar tendon; will have surgery and is out for the rest of the season.
Asked about his injury status; Quinn did not have an update and said more information would come Monday.
Quinn said the offense will get more into its flow as Daniels gets back, implying he is still working back to full health.

signals.claim: Will likely be elevated into a bigger role at receiver after McLaurin's injury, as he has already been once this season.
signals.note: With McLaurin out, Jefferson is a leading candidate to pick up targets and deep-threat snaps.

signals.claim: Expects Daniels to run more keepers and out-of-pocket plays off the play-action game as he develops.
signals.note: More designed runs and scramble opportunities would boost Daniels' rushing floor and fantasy ceiling.

topics.detail: Quinn said the line's performance was below the team's standard, especially in pass protection, and that he will keep trying combinations on the interior.
Quinn wants better pre-snap urgency and call communication and fewer explosive pass plays allowed, especially on first and second down.
Changes are expected to be smaller tweaks and streamlining rather than a new system or new plays, with a focus on being more decisive and precise.
Quinn said the team's plus-six turnover differential is not yet translating to wins and that the complementary football needs to be sharper.
